subnet_formula: (nodes + max surge) + ((nodes + max surge) * max pods per node)
notes: In a flat network model every pod takes a real address out of a virtual network subnet, so the demand is nodes x pods and not nodes. Azure CNI in node subnet mode (network_plugin = azure with no network_plugin_mode) takes both nodes and pods from the node subnet; Azure CNI pod subnet mode takes nodes from one subnet and pods from another. Azure CNI Overlay and kubenet give pods addresses from a separate CIDR that never touches the virtual network, so subnet exhaustion is not a question for them and the rule stays silent. Defaults differ by deployment path: the Azure CLI and ARM/portal have historically disagreed, and this table takes the values from the 'Maximum pods per node' table on the page above. A subnet CIDR cannot be resized once resources are deployed in it, and maxPods cannot be raised on an existing node pool: the only fix is a new node pool or a new cluster.
surge_notes: The documented formula adds the upgrade surge nodes, because a rolling upgrade briefly runs an extra node and its full complement of pods. Terraform states max surge in upgrade_settings.max_surge as either a count or a percentage, and the rule ignores it when absent so that demand is understated rather than overstated.
